High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Dilip Parihar - Panel Lawyer for respondent-State.
Record of the Court below is received.
Heard on the question of admission.
Admit.
Also heard on I.A. No.1047/2024, which is an application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant Jamuna Prasad Soni.

The appellant has been convicted by the trial Court under Sections 420, 467 r/w Section 120-B, 468 r/w Section 120-B and Section 471 r/w Section 120-B of IPC and sentenced him to undergo R.I. for 5 years for each offences with fine of Rs.25,000/- for each offences with default stipulations.
I t is contended by the counsel that the trial Court has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record while convicting the appellant for the aforesaid offences.
As per prosecution, co- accused Parsadhi by impersonation, projected himself to be complainant Basanta Kachi and executed a Power of Attorney in favour of co-accused Nirbhay Singh.

On the basis of said Power of Attorney, complainant Santosh Sharma (PW-3) was persuaded to execute the sale-deed and accordingly, a sale-deed was executed in favour of co-accused Parsadhi, in which,
other co- accused implicated as according to prosecution, they approached complainant Santosh Sharma (PW-3) who stated that in order to discuss the alienation of property in question, accused persons came to his office and later on, the Power of Attorney verified and it was found to be valid.
Thereafter, the sale deed was executed, however, when the sale deed was shown to Patwari concerned, it was informed to the complainant that the said sale deed was forged.

It is further contended by the counsel that so far as the Power of Attorney, Agreement and sale deed are concerned, in none of the documents, the signature of present appellant-Jamuna Prasad Soni are there.

The appellant was neither executor nor witness to the said documents, therefore, the Jamuna Prasad Soni vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146632556/

sentences.text: 1 implication of the present appellant is only based on the fact that he came to the office of complainant when co-accused persons have gone to discuss the alienation of the property in question.
It is also contended by the counsel that appellant is aged about 60 years and has suffered two years and nine months in custody as of now as against sentence of 5 years.
There is material contradictions and omissions in the evidence of witnesses.
This appeal is of the year 2024 and final hearing of this appeal will take considerable time.
There is fair chances of the appellant to succeed in the appeal.
Under these circumstances, if the sentence of the appellant is not suspended, purpose to file this appeal will be futile.
Therefore, the custodial sentence of the appellants be suspended and he be released on bail.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent has opposed the prayer and while taking this Court to paragraphs 49 and 55 of the judgment submits that there is a conviction of the appellant under Section 120-B of IPC as well, therefore, he was also part of the conspiracy.
It is contended by the counsel that the appellant has played active role and accordingly, he has been rightly convicted under the aforesaid sections.
Thus, counsel submits that the application for suspension of sentence deserves to be rejected.
Heard the rival submissions and perused the record.

It is evident that in testimony of Santosh Sharma (PW-3) he deposed that all co-accused including present appellant (Jamuna Prasad Soni) came to his office where the discussion as regards the property in question had taken place and later on, upon verification of the concerned Power of Attorney, the sale deed was executed.

It is undisputed that so far as the Power of Attorney,
agreement and sale deed are concerned, all the documents do not contain signature of present appellant i.e. Jamuna Prasad Soni.

Therefore, taking into consideration the aforesaid aspect and also the period of incarceration of appellant already suffered by him as well as his age, this Court deem it proper to suspend the jail sentence of the appellant.
Accordingly, IA No.1047/2024 is allowed.

The execution of jail sentence of appellant-Jamuna Prasad Soni is hereby suspended subject to depositing the fine amount, (if not already deposited) and on his furnishing a personal bond to a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court with a further direction to appear before the trial Court on 20.05.2024 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
C.C. as per rules.
